title: Behavioural Interview Question Bank
content:
# Behavioural Interview Question Bank

Use STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Keep answers under two minutes. Prepare stories for teamwork, conflict, failure, leadership, and a tight deadline.

title: Behavioural Interview Question Bank
content:
Example: a group project where a teammate missed a deadline. Situation and task first, then what YOU did (re-planned tasks, spoke privately, documented work), then the result (submitted on time, grade, what you would do next time).

Common prompts: "Tell me about a time you failed." "Describe a conflict in a team." "When did you learn a tool quickly?" Practise out loud. Do not memorise a script word for word.

title: Careers in Data Science
content:
# Careers in Data Science

Analyst, data scientist, and machine learning engineer are different jobs. Analysts clean data and explain trends. Data scientists prototype models and experiments. ML engineers put models into production with monitoring.

For a computer science graduate in Nairobi, a realistic first role is data analyst or junior ML engineer if you have Python, SQL, and one portfolio project.

title: Careers in Data Science
content:
A master's is not required for many analyst roles. It helps for research-heavy ML. Salaries vary widely; treat unofficial figures as unverified until you check a primary source.

Build a small end-to-end project: dataset, notebook, simple model, short write-up of limitations.

title: Cover Letter Writing Guide
content:
# Cover Letter Writing Guide

A cover letter should be under 300 words. Paragraph 1: the role and why this organisation. Paragraph 2: one project that maps to their needs. Paragraph 3: availability and a clear ask for an interview.

Do not repeat the CV. Translate coursework into their problem. For a data internship, a class dashboard becomes "I cleaned 2,000 rows and presented trends to a supervisor."

title: Cover Letter Writing Guide
content: Address a named hiring manager when you can. Close with thanks and your phone number. For Kenyan graduate schemes, mention when you can start and that you can work on-site if required.

title: Building a Portfolio Website
content:
# Building a Portfolio Website

Recruiters spend under two minutes on a student site. Show two or three projects, not ten. Each project needs a problem, what you built, the stack, and a link to code or a demo.

Use a simple layout: name, course (for example BSc Computer Science, Strathmore), one-line goal, then projects. Host on GitHub Pages.

title: Building a Portfolio Website
content: Do not hide the GitHub link. Include one project that matches the jobs you want (API, data analysis, or a small ML demo). Write in plain English, not buzzwords.

title: Software Engineer CV Template
content:
# Software Engineer CV Template

A strong internship or graduate CV for computer science students is one page. Lead with education (course, expected graduation, relevant modules), then 2–3 projects with impact, then skills, then experience.

Write bullets as action + tool + result. Example: "Built a REST API in Python and FastAPI that cut manual report time from 3 hours to 15 minutes." Avoid listing duties only.

title: Software Engineer CV Template
content:
Match the job description: if the posting asks for Git, SQL, and teamwork, those words should appear honestly in your projects. Recruiters in Nairobi and remote teams scan for that overlap in seconds.

Include a GitHub or portfolio link. Do not attach a photo. Keep margins readable and use a single font.

title: Technical Interview Practice: Algorithms
content:
# Technical Interview Practice: Algorithms

Coding screens usually mix arrays, hash maps, strings, and simple graphs. Talk while you think: restate the problem, give an example, state time complexity, then code.

Start with a brute-force idea, then improve. For internships, correct and clear code beats a clever one-liner you cannot explain.

title: Technical Interview Practice: Algorithms
content: Practise: two-sum, reverse a linked list, BFS on a grid, and SQL group-by. After each problem, write the Big-O. If you stall, say what you would test next rather than going silent.

**Question:** What is the difference between compilation and interpretation?

Compilation translates source code into machine code creating an executable file. Interpretation translates and executes code line by line without an executable.

**Question:** How do you protect against session fixation attacks?

**Difficulty Level:** Medium

**Concept & Model Answer:**

**Concept & Model Answer:**
Least privilege limits access rights; defense in depth layers security. Both minimize attack surfaces and provide redundancy.
